headline: Florida Nuclear Plant Becomes Unlikely Refuge for Endangered Crocodiles
meta_description: A Florida nuclear plant's cooling canals have become a thriving nursery for American crocodiles, with 606 hatchlings recorded last season—the highest count in…
summary_short: Cooling canals at a Florida nuclear facility have unexpectedly become a major breeding ground for once-endangered American crocodiles, setting a historic record.
body:
A Florida nuclear plant's cooling canals have become a major nursery for once-endangered American crocodiles. Last season, researchers counted 606 hatchlings—the highest total in the program's 47-year history.

The unlikely success story reveals how industrial infrastructure, when managed thoughtfully, can support wildlife recovery. The warm-water environment created by the plant's cooling system has proven ideal for crocodile reproduction, transforming what might have been dismissed as a mere industrial byproduct into critical habitat.

This milestone reflects decades of dedicated conservation work. The sustained increase in hatchling numbers demonstrates that American crocodiles, once driven to the brink of extinction, are slowly reclaiming a foothold in Florida waters—even in the shadow of human development.
quick_facts: 606 crocodile hatchlings recorded in last breeding season
Highest count in the program's 47-year history
Nuclear plant cooling canals now serve as major nursery
American crocodiles once endangered, now recovering
